personality_one_liner: A highly reliable, crisp, and high-contrast utility app that feels premium for residents while operating with strict precision for security guards.

spacing.rule: Adhere to strict iOS-native margins (typically 16pt outer) and ensure large 44x44pt minimum touch targets for all interactive elements, especially crucial for the guard view in varied outdoor lighting.

do's: Use blur on the bottom tab bar and sticky headers over scrollable feeds (like the resident's active passes list).
Apply frosted glass overlays over the main hero architecture imagery on the login screen.
dont's: Do not use glass effects on the Guard Scanner or Scan Result screens; these must remain solid, high-contrast, and instantly readable in harsh outdoor daylight.

screens.name: Login

states.loading: Centered native spinner over the login form.
states.error: Inline red validation text under inputs.

screens.layout: Full-bleed architectural hero image at the top with a gradient scrim (top to bottom). A clean, white floating card at the bottom (using border-radius top-left/right) housing the login form. Include segmented control or plain text links to toggle between Resident, Guard, and Admin roles.

screens.name: Resident Dashboard
screens.purpose: Overview of visitor activity and quick access to create new passes.

states.loading: Skeleton loaders for the recent visitor list.
states.empty: Illustration of a secure gate with 'No active passes' and a prominent 'Invite Visitor' button.
states.error: Card displaying 'Unable to load passes' with a 'Retry' button.

screens.layout: Dashboard pattern. Top sticky header with Resident greeting and unread notifications badge. A large, prominent 'Invite Visitor' primary CTA card at the top of the scroll view. Below: a section for 'Active Passes' (horizontal scroll or stacked cards) and 'Unexpected Visitor Requests' (actionable cards with Approve/Reject).

screens.name: QR Pass Preview
screens.purpose: Displays the generated QR code for sharing and pass management.

states.loading: Spinner centered on the QR code slot.

screens.layout: Centered, high-contrast QR code contained within a bordered, elevated card (shadow tier 2). Below the code: pass validity details (time-window, one-time). A sticky primary CTA at the bottom using phone share sheet ('Share Pass'), and a secondary destructive text button ('Revoke Pass').

screens.name: Guard Scanner
screens.purpose: Full-screen camera utility for guards to scan incoming visitor QR codes.

states.error: Fallback message 'Camera permission denied' with a button to open settings, plus manual lookup option.

screens.layout: Camera view takes up the entire screen. A dark translucent overlay with a clear square cutout in the center guides the scan. Floating pill at the top shows offline status ('Offline: 5 Pending Syncs' in warning color). Floating bottom panel with a large 'Manual Lookup' button.

screens.name: Scan Result
screens.purpose: Immediate, unambiguous access decision feedback for guards.

states.error: N/A - the entire screen acts as the status.

screens.layout: FULL SCREEN status overlay. Background color strictly maps to result: Solid Success (Green), Solid Error (Red), or Solid Warning (Orange). Large, bold typography ('ACCESS GRANTED' / 'DENIED' / 'EXPIRED'). In the center, a card containing the visitor's photo (for visual ID check), name, and host resident details. Large 'Dismiss' button at the bottom.

screens.name: Admin Overview
screens.purpose: High-level metrics, charts, and system management for estate admins.

states.loading: Skeleton UI for charts and metric cards.
states.error: Toast or inline alert indicating sync failure.

screens.layout: Grid of key metric cards (Entries Today, Denied Entries, Active Passes). Below: A chart (using a library like react-native-chart-kit) showing visitor traffic. Sections for 'Active Guards' and 'Recent Security Incidents'. Use iOS grouped list styling (surfaceSecondary background with surface cards) for dense data presentation.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly avoid any blues, purples, or navys in the UI. Stick to the predefined Charcoal/Black brand palette with strict iOS system colors for status (Green, Orange, Red).
Implement role-based routing (Resident vs. Guard vs. Admin) immediately after login. Do not mix their navigation stacks.
For the Guard role, the root screen must be the full-screen QR scanner (using expo-camera). It must support offline scanning mode, caching results locally and displaying an offline sync badge.
The Guard Scan Result screen must fill the entire screen with the solid status color (success/warning/error) as its background. This is a critical requirement for outdoor daylight readability.
When a visitor's pass is generated, use React Native's `Share` API to trigger the native phone share sheet instead of a custom sharing UI.
Ensure the Resident Dashboard prominently displays unexpected visitor requests (Approve/Reject) at the top of the feed to reduce friction.
